notes: Version 1.3. The observable saturation rank is not invariant under a global rescaling of the observable: its exponent is ratio-invariant but the threshold base is not, so it scales as lambda^(1/delta); it is defined for the canonical normalisation of O19 and the former invariance claim is withdrawn. The abstract no longer states that the programme identified the pair observable as the relevant quantity for the lepton mass hierarchy: no O-series result establishes that link. The threshold Sigma_c(n_3)=3 is a supplied selection rule (O24). The shell-alignment conjecture remains open: O22 places the Born-Infeld saturation depth on a shell but does not identify it with the O21 rank. The single q=61 value of Table 1 (n_3^obs = 4.80, distance 0.20) is withdrawn: its own O12 data reproduce the printed exponent and bracket but give n_3^obs = 3.65 (distance 0.35), and the O25 data give 3.51 (distance 0.50), both for non-canonical observables; and the cumulative-span reading of the threshold is shown inconsistent with a decreasing observable.
